description: 20 fixed cases covering correctness, faithfulness, completeness and instruction following.

cases.system_prompt: Answer for a beginner in 2-3 sentences.
cases.model_output_a: Supervised learning trains a model on labelled input-output examples so it can learn a mapping and predict outputs for new inputs.
cases.model_output_b: Supervised learning learns from labelled examples. For example, it can learn to classify emails as spam or not spam.
cases.expected_output: Supervised learning learns from labelled input-output examples to predict outputs for new inputs.

cases.model_output_a: Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too closely, including noise, so training performance is high but performance on unseen data is poor.
cases.model_output_b: Overfitting means the model is too simple and cannot learn the training pattern.
cases.expected_output: Overfitting occurs when a model fits training data too closely and generalizes poorly to unseen data.

cases.model_output_a: An LLM is a large language model trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate natural language. It predicts likely token sequences from context.
cases.model_output_b: An LLM is a database that stores every answer people have written.
cases.expected_output: An LLM is a machine-learning model trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language.

cases.model_output_a: A train/test split lets us train on one portion of data and evaluate generalization on unseen data.
cases.model_output_b: It is mainly used to make the training dataset larger.
cases.expected_output: The split separates training data from unseen test data so generalization can be evaluated.

cases.model_output_a: Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are actually positive: TP / (TP + FP).
cases.model_output_b: Precision is the fraction of actual positives that the classifier correctly identifies: TP / (TP + FN).
cases.expected_output: Precision = TP / (TP + FP), measuring how many predicted positives are truly positive.

cases.model_output_a: An embedding represents an item such as text as a numerical vector that captures useful semantic relationships.
cases.model_output_b: An embedding is a compressed image file.
cases.expected_output: An embedding is a numerical vector representation that captures semantic or other useful features.

cases.input: What does temperature control in text generation?
cases.model_output_a: Temperature changes the randomness of token selection. Higher values generally make outputs more varied, while lower values make them more deterministic.
cases.model_output_b: Temperature controls the physical temperature of the GPU.
cases.expected_output: Temperature controls randomness in token sampling; higher values generally increase variation.

cases.model_output_a: Data leakage occurs when information unavailable at prediction time is accidentally used during training or evaluation, causing overly optimistic results.
cases.model_output_b: Data leakage is when a dataset is stored in the cloud.
cases.expected_output: Data leakage occurs when information that should be unavailable is used during training or evaluation.

cases.system_prompt: Give the formula and a one-sentence explanation.
cases.model_output_a: Recall is TP / (TP + FN), the fraction of actual positive cases that were correctly identified.
cases.model_output_b: Recall is TP / (TP + FP), the fraction of predicted positives that are correct.
cases.expected_output: Recall = TP / (TP + FN), measuring how many actual positives are found.

cases.model_output_a: A confusion matrix summarizes classification results using true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives.
cases.model_output_b: A confusion matrix is a matrix used only to store model weights.
cases.expected_output: A confusion matrix summarizes TP, TN, FP, and FN classification outcomes.

cases.model_output_a: Feature scaling can put variables on comparable numerical ranges, which can help distance-based and gradient-based algorithms behave better.
cases.model_output_b: Normalization always improves every machine-learning model and is mandatory.
cases.expected_output: Feature scaling puts variables on comparable ranges and can improve optimization or distance calculations for some algorithms.

cases.model_output_a: Cross-validation repeatedly splits data into training and validation portions so model performance can be estimated more reliably.
cases.model_output_b: Cross-validation means validating the final model only once on its training data.
cases.expected_output: Cross-validation evaluates a model across multiple train-validation splits to estimate generalization.

cases.model_output_a: An API is an interface that lets one software component request data or functionality from another using defined rules.
cases.model_output_b: An API is a type of database that stores passwords.
cases.expected_output: An API defines how software components communicate and request data or actions.

cases.model_output_a: RAG retrieves relevant external documents and gives them to a language model as context before generation. This can improve grounding and allow answers to use a changing knowledge source.
cases.model_output_b: RAG means the language model permanently memorizes every document in a database.
cases.expected_output: RAG retrieves relevant external context and supplies it to a generator so the answer can be grounded in retrieved information.

cases.model_output_a: A validation set is used during development to compare configurations or tune choices without using the final test set.
cases.model_output_b: A validation set is the same thing as the training set and is used to memorize labels.
cases.expected_output: A validation set supports model or hyperparameter decisions while keeping the final test set separate.

cases.input: What is hallucination in an LLM?
cases.model_output_a: An LLM hallucination is a generated claim that is unsupported, fabricated, or inconsistent with the available evidence.
cases.model_output_b: Hallucination means an LLM is thinking like a human and therefore has consciousness.
cases.expected_output: An LLM hallucination is an unsupported or fabricated generated claim.

cases.model_output_a: Cosine similarity compares the angle between two vectors, commonly using their normalized dot product. A larger value generally means greater directional similarity.
cases.model_output_b: Cosine similarity is the Euclidean distance between two database rows.
cases.expected_output: Cosine similarity measures directional similarity between vectors using their normalized dot product.

cases.model_output_a: An idempotent operation can be repeated without changing the final result after the first successful application. For example, replacing a resource with the same representation can be idempotent.
cases.model_output_b: An idempotent operation must always produce a random result each time.
cases.expected_output: An idempotent operation can be repeated without changing the final state after the first successful application.

cases.model_output_a: Evaluation logs make prompts, raw responses, scores, latency, and failures auditable and help reproduce or debug regressions.
cases.model_output_b: Logging is unnecessary because model outputs are always deterministic.
cases.expected_output: Logs provide an audit trail for prompts, responses, scores, latency, and failures.

cases.input: When should a human review an LLM judge decision?
cases.model_output_a: Human review is appropriate for borderline scores, safety-sensitive failures, high-impact decisions, or cases where automated judge reliability is uncertain.
cases.model_output_b: A human should never review an LLM judge because the judge is always correct.
cases.expected_output: Human review should remain available for borderline, high-impact, safety-sensitive, or unreliable automated decisions.
